newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via weekend or 6-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via weekend or 6-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves into the banking system via system repurchase agreements Friday, although the term is subject to debate, analysts said.

With a projected $5 billion to $6 billion average daily add need seen for the rest of the reserve period -- which ends Wednesday -- analysts said the Fed will either do over the weekend system RPs or six-day system RPs.
Marc Wanshel, Fed watcher at J.P. Morgan & Co, said that with the overnight system RPs from Thursday coming off the books today, an operation is required this session.
Analysts also said the 14-day system RPs done last week amounted to only $2 billion, which was not enough to cover the current add need.
On Thursday the Fed entered the market an hour and a half early to combat pressure on federal funds.

Funds were under pressure once again on Friday. Funds opened at 5-7/16 percent and then edged up to 5-9/16. Maturing cash management bills are said to be causing the pressure. The market is on alert for another early operation.
With the add need rising, the possibility of a bill pass increases. Such an operation could come as early as today, analysts said.
